scribeTiers.scribeName: The Eyewitness of the Holy Mount
Newe Heauens and a Newe Earth

characters.name: Simon Peter
characters.scribeTier: The Eyewitness of the Holy Mount
characters.perkNote: Naming collision: multiple NT figures named Simon (Simon the Zealot, Simon the brother of Jesus, Simon of Cyrene, Simon the tanner, Simon Magus) - this epistle's author is unambiguously 'Simon Peter a seruant and an Apostle of Iesus Christ' per 1:1. Id is Geneva-translation- and book-scoped, kept separate from both the KJV '2Peter.json' index's 'peter_2peter' and from any Geneva Gospel/Acts Peter entries, per this project's per-book-per-translation manager convention.

verses.note: Opens 'Simon Peter a seruant and an Apostle of Iesus Christ, to you which haue obteined like precious faith with vs by the righteousnesse of our God and Sauiour Iesus Christ' - identical in substance to the standard KJV opening, spelled in the Geneva Bible's distinctive 1560 orthography.

Peter resolves not to be negligent in reminding them, 'as long as I am in this tabernacle,' knowing 'the time is at hand that I must lay downe this my tabernacle, euen as our Lord Iesus Christ hath shewed me,' and endeavours that they be able to remember these things 'after my departing.'

Peter grounds his teaching in eyewitness testimony rather than 'deceiuable fables' - he saw Christ's majesty personally and heard the voice from 'that excellent glory' declare 'This is my beloued Sonne, in whom I am well pleased,' a voice heard 'when it came from heauen, being with him in the Holy mount.'

Points to 'a most sure worde of the Prophets... as vnto a light that shineth in a darke place,' teaching that 'no prophecie of the Scripture is of any priuate interpretation... but holy men of God spake as they were moued by the holy Ghost.'

Identifies this as 'This seconde Epistle I nowe write vnto you, beloued,' written to stirre up their pure minds by remembrance of the words of the holy Prophets and 'the commandement of vs the Apostles of the Lord and Sauiour.'

Closes warning them not to be 'plucked away with the errour of the wicked' but to 'grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Sauiour Iesus Christ: to him be glory both now and for euermore. Amen.'

funFacts: Geneva renders Peter's body-as-tent image 'this my tabernacle' (1:13-14), identical in sense to the KJV phrasing.

1:16-18 is one of the clearest first-person eyewitness claims to the Transfiguration in the New Testament, spoken in Peter's own voice rather than narrated about him - unchanged in the Geneva text from the standard reading.

characters.name: Ioyne Vertue With Your Faith
characters.purpose: Instructs believers to 'giue euen all diligence' to add to their faith a progressive chain - vertue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godlines, brotherly kindnes, loue - so that they be neither idle nor vnfruitfull, and so 'make your calling and election sure'; warns that lacking these things leaves a man 'blinde, and can not see farre off,' having forgotten his cleansing from his old sins.

verses.note: The chain to be joined one to another: faith, vertue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godlines, brotherly kindnes, loue.

Having these things in abundance keeps a believer fruitful 'in the acknowledging of our Lord Iesus Christ'; lacking them, he 'is blinde, and can not see farre off, and hath forgotten that he was purged from his olde sinnes.'

Exhorts them to 'giue rather diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye doe these things, ye shall neuer fall,' promising 'an entring... ministred vnto you aboundantly into the euerlasting kingdome of our Lord and Sauiour Iesus Christ.'

characters.name: Welles Without Water
characters.purpose: Warns that 'false prophets also among the people' foreshadow 'false teachers among you: which priuily shall bring in damnable heresies, euen denying the Lord, that hath bought them,' exploiting believers 'through couetousnes... with fained words'; grounds God's certain pattern of judgment and deliverance in three Old Testament examples (the sinning angels, the Flood, Sodom and Gomorrah with Lot's deliverance), then denounces the false teachers themselves as bold, self-willed, and doomed.

verses.note: False teachers foretold, who 'priuily shall bring in damnable heresies,' whose 'condemnation long since resteth not, and their destruction slumbreth not.'
'God spared not the Angels that had sinned, but cast them downe into hell, and deliuered them into chaines of darkenes, to be kept vnto damnation.'

God 'saued Noe the eight person a preacher of righteousnesse' amid the Flood upon 'the world of the vngodly' - the text itself gives only the number eight and does not name or enumerate the other seven, that detail comes from Genesis, not from this book's own wording. Sodom and Gomorrhe were turned 'into ashes,' made 'an ensample vnto them that after should liue vngodly.'

God 'deliuered iust Loth vexed with the vncleanly conuersation of the wicked,' proof 'the Lord knoweth to deliuer the godly out of tentation, and to reserue the vniust vnto the day of iudgement vnder punishment.'
The false teachers likened to 'naturall brute beasts,' called 'Spottes... and blottes,' having 'eyes full of adulterie' and 'heartes exercised with couetousnesse.'
Compares them to Balaam, 'the sonne of Bosor, which loued the wages of vnrighteousnes,' rebuked when 'the dumme beast speaking with mans voyce, forbade the foolishnesse of the Prophet.'
Called 'welles without water, and cloudes caried about with a tempest, to whome the blacke darkenes is reserued for euer.'
Warns that a relapsed believer's 'latter ende is worse... then the beginning,' illustrated by 'The dogge is returned to his owne vomit: and, The sowe that was washed, to the wallowing in the myre.'

funFacts: Verse 2:8 embeds its clarifying aside about Lot's vexed righteous soul directly in the main text inside parentheses ('(For he being righteous...)') rather than as a separate marginal note - a distinctively Genevan editorial touch, since the Geneva Bible is best known for its extensive marginal annotation apparatus.

characters.name: Newe Heauens and a Newe Earth
characters.scribeTier: Newe Heauens and a Newe Earth
characters.purpose: Answers 'mockers' in the last days who ask 'Where is the promise of his comming?', explains that with the Lord 'one day... [is] as a thousande yeeres, and a thousande yeeres as one day' and that his seeming slackness is patience 'toward vs,' and describes 'the day of the Lord' coming 'as a thiefe in the night' in which the heauens and elements shall be dissolved with fire - grounding the promise of 'newe heauens, and a newe earth... wherein dwelleth righteousnesse' and exhorting diligence to be found 'in peace, without spot and blamelesse.'

verses.note: 'Mockers' in the last days, walking after their own lusts, ask 'Where is the promise of his comming? for since the fathers died, all things continue alike from the beginning of the creation.'
Recalls 'the worlde that then was, perished, ouerflowed with the water'; the present heavens and earth 'are kept by the same word in store, and reserued vnto fire against the day of condemnation.'
'One day is with the Lord, as a thousande yeeres, and a thousande yeeres as one day'; the Lord 'is pacient toward vs, and would haue no man to perish, but would all men to come to repentance.'
'The day of the Lord will come as a thiefe in the night,' the heauens passing away 'with a noyse,' the elements melting 'with heate,' the earth and its works 'burnt vp.'

Exhorts 'holy conuersation and godlinesse' while 'looking for, and hasting vnto the comming of that day of God,' anticipating 'newe heauens, and a newe earth, according to his promise, wherein dwelleth righteousnesse.'
Exhorts diligence 'that ye may be found of him in peace, without spot and blamelesse.'

Notes 'the long suffering of our Lord is saluation, euen as our beloued brother Paul according to the wisedome giuen vnto him wrote to you,' acknowledging some things in his epistles 'are hard to be vnderstand, which they that are vnlearned and vnstable, wrest... vnto their owne destruction.'

characters.name: Iesus Christ (referenced)
characters.perkNote: Iesus is named or titled throughout this epistle (1:1, 1:8, 1:11, 1:14, 1:16-18, 2:1, 2:20, 3:2, 3:18), but per this project's personally-embodied vs. pure-transmission test he does not himself act within this book's own scene - it is Peter recalling past events (including the Transfiguration) and exhorting the recipients, not a narrated episode in which Jesus is directly present. Logged as a lightweight named reference, consistent with the KJV '2Peter.json' index's own treatment. Jesus's full, independent manager tier(s) belong to the Geneva Gospels once indexed, per this project's per-Gospel-per-translation convention, not to this epistle.

verses.note: Peter identifies himself as 'a seruant and an Apostle of Iesus Christ,' writing to those who 'haue obteined like precious faith... by the righteousnesse of our God and Sauiour Iesus Christ.'
Fruitfulness described as being 'in the acknowledging of our Lord Iesus Christ,' with an abundant entrance promised into 'the euerlasting kingdome of our Lord and Sauiour Iesus Christ.'
Peter says his approaching death was shown to him 'euen as our Lord Iesus Christ hath shewed me.'
Peter recalls witnessing Christ's majesty 'in the Holy mount,' where a voice from 'that excellent glory' declared 'This is my beloued Sonne, in whom I am well pleased.'
False teachers described as 'denying the Lord, that hath bought them.'
Escape from the world's filthiness comes 'through the acknowledging of the Lord, and of the Sauiour Iesus Christ.'
Referenced via 'the commandement of vs the Apostles of the Lord and Sauiour.'
Closing exhortation to 'grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Sauiour Iesus Christ: to him be glory both now and for euermore. Amen.'

characters.name: Paul (referenced)
characters.perkNote: Only a brief epistolary reference in 3:15-16 - Paul is not personally embodied acting within this book's own scene, so he is logged as a lightweight named reference rather than a full manager tier, matching the KJV index's own treatment. His own full manager tier(s) are expected once the Geneva Acts/Pauline epistles are indexed.

verses.note: Called 'our beloued brother Paul,' who wrote to them 'according to the wisedome giuen vnto him'; some of his writing is 'hard to be vnderstand, which they that are vnlearned and vnstable, wrest, as they do also other Scriptures vnto their owne destruction.'

genealogyLists.note: Bulk references to already-indexed Old Testament figures/groups cited in chapter 2 purely as illustrative examples of divine judgment or deliverance - not new characters appearing in this book's own narrative, so not given full character entries here.

angels_that_sinned.note: 'The Angels that had sinned,' cast downe into hell and 'deliuered them into chaines of darkenes, to be kept vnto damnation' - the text does not name or individually differentiate them.

the_flood_and_noah.note: References the Flood and 'Noe the eight person, a preacher of righteousnesse,' saved when God 'brought in the flood vpon the world of the vngodly' - see Noah's full entry once the Geneva Genesis index exists.

sodom_and_gomorrhe.note: 'The cities of Sodom and Gomorrhe' turned 'into ashes,' made 'an ensample vnto them that after should liue vngodly' - see the Geneva Genesis index.

lot.note: 'Iust Loth vexed with the vncleanly conuersation of the wicked' and delivered by God out of Sodom - see Lot's full entry once the Geneva Genesis index exists.

balaam.note: Balaam, called here 'the sonne of Bosor' (2:15), matching the same patronymic-spelling variant already flagged in the KJV index against 'son of Beor' in Numbers - a name-form variant, not a different person; rebuked when 'the dumme beast speaking with mans voyce, forbade the foolishnesse of the Prophet.' See Balaam's full entry once the Geneva Numbers index exists.

notes: This translation's actual extracted text (E:/Unity/Clicker_Genesis/Assets/Resources/Verses/Geneva/2_peter_73.json) was read in full before drafting. Geneva's 2 Peter is, content-wise, essentially identical to the standard 3-chapter/61-verse text most readers know as KJV's 2 Peter - no structural or canonical differences were found (unlike, e.g., the Ethiopian Bible's genuinely different 9-chapter Ezra) - the differences here are entirely orthographic/lexical, native to the 1560 Geneva translation itself: 'Iesus' for Jesus, 'Sauiour' for Saviour, 'vertue'/'vs'/'haue'/'giue' for virtue/us/have/give, 'godlines' for godliness, 'welles' for wells, 'iust Loth' for 'just Lot,' 'the eight person' for 'the eighth person,' 'sonne of Bosor' for 'son of Bosor,' 'priuate interpretation' for 'private interpretation.' Structurally the epistle is almost entirely exhortation and warning rather than narrative, so - exactly as in the parallel KJV index - only one figure, Peter himself, meets the personally-embodied test for a full manager tier (he writes as an eyewitness of the Transfiguration, speaks of his own approaching death, and identifies this as his second letter to the recipients). The epistle's other heavy content blocks are law/theme tiers: the ladder of virtue to be joined to faith (1:5-11), the extended denunciation of false teachers grounded in three Old Testament judgment/deliverance examples (chapter 2), and the day of the Lord together with the promise of new heavens and a new earth (chapter 3). Iesus Christ and Paul are both referenced repeatedly (Iesus) or in passing (Paul, 3:15-16) without personally acting within this book's own scene, so both are logged as lightweight role:'named' entries rather than full manager tiers, applying the personally-embodied-vs-pure-transmission test consistently; Iesus's own full, independent manager tier(s) belong to the Geneva Gospels once indexed, per this project's per-Gospel-per-translation convention. The Old Testament figures cited in chapter 2 (the sinning angels, Noah and the Flood, Sodom and Gomorrah, Lot, Balaam) are illustrative references to figures who belong to the eventual Geneva Old Testament index, not new characters in this book's own narrative, so they sit in genealogyLists rather than as duplicated full entries - the text itself states only that Noah was saved as 'the eight person' without itself naming or enumerating the other seven, flagged as drawn from Genesis rather than presented as this book's own stated content. Naming-collision note: this epistle's author is unambiguously 'Simon Peter' the apostle (1:1), distinct from every other NT figure named Simon (Simon the Zealot, Simon the brother of Jesus, Simon of Cyrene, Simon the tanner, Simon Magus) - flagged even though only one Simon appears in this particular book, since this character will sit alongside those other Simons project-wide; his id is kept translation- and book-scoped ('peter_geneva_2peter'), separate from the existing KJV '2Peter.json' index's 'peter_2peter' and from any future Geneva Gospel/Acts Peter entries, following this project's per-book-per-translation manager convention. One distinctive Geneva editorial feature worth flagging for future translation-comparison UI: verse 2:8 embeds a clarifying aside about Lot's vexed righteous soul directly in the main text inside parentheses, a small window into the Geneva Bible's well-known marginal-annotation tradition surfacing inline rather than in a true margin. All direct scripture quotations in this file were checked against the actual read text file, not reconstructed from memory of the KJV wording.
